previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old pregnant woman with a history of bipolar disorder and borderline personality traits was admitted due to severe depressive episode with psychotic features and suicidal ideation. She presented with profound sadness, auditory hallucinations, and psychomotor agitation. During her 7-day stay, she was found to have hyponatremia, hypothyroidism, anemia, and mild acidosis, all managed supportively. She tested negative for sexually transmitted infections. After stabilization, she underwent a single session of unilateral electroconvulsive therapy, which led to marked improvement in mood and resolution of psychotic symptoms. She was discharged in stable condition with a plan for ongoing outpatient ECT, psychiatric follow-up, and continuation of prenatal care with OB and mental health providers.
